topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the lecture's focus on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Tissue Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbial and cellular danger signals through pattern recognition receptors, toll-like receptor signaling cascades, and the inflammasome complex.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated tissue sentinel cells stimulate endothelial adhesion flags to mediate the rolling, extravasation, and chemotactic recruitment of circulating leukocytes to the infection site.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Antigen Transport to Lymph Nodes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how dendritic cells transport antigens away from the infection site through the lymphatic drainage network to initiate adaptive immune priming in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Systemic Inflammatory Pathology and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the life-threatening clinical consequences that occur when excessive inflammatory cytokine production triggers uncontrolled systemic vasodilation and sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, how damaged tissue is repaired, and the outcomes when inflammatory responses become chronic or form granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic for the following lecture.
